title: nymphaea alba var. urceolata
intro: Nymphaea alba var. urceolata, commonly known as the white water lily, is a type of aquatic plant that belongs to the Nymphaea genus. This plant has been traditionally used in folk medicine to treat various health conditions, including fever, rheumatism, and skin irritations, due to its health benefits such as anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties. The therapeutic actions of Nymphaea alba var. urceolata include antioxidant, antihistaminic, and anxiolytic effects, making it a potential treatment for anxiety disorders and other conditions. The bioactive constituents of this plant include alkaloids, flavonoids, and saponins, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
